Hungarian vowel harmony in a wug test

Source: R/data.R
hungarian_harmony.Rd

50 Hungarian speakers choose between a back (-nak) and a front (-nek) dative suffix for 84 nonce stems. Stems with only back vowels take back suffixes and stems with front rounded vowels front ones. Stems with a back vowel followed by neutral vowels vary: the lower the last neutral vowel (i > é > e), the more front suffixes (the Height Effect), and two neutral vowels give more front suffixes than one (the Count Effect).

Usage

hungarian_harmony

Format

A tibble with 4200 rows and 6 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P50.

item

Item ID, i01 to i84.

stem_type

Vowels of the stem: "B" (back), "F" (front rounded), "N" (neutral only), "Bi", "Bé", "Be" (back vowel plus one neutral vowel) or "BNN" (back vowel plus two neutral vowels).

n_neutral

Number of neutral vowels after the last back vowel.

last_vowel

Last vowel of the stem: "back", "front rounded", "high", "mid" or "low".

suffix

"back" or "front".

Source

data-raw/hungarian_harmony.R

Details

True model: the probability of a back suffix is 0.97 (B), 0.03 (F), 0.08 (N), 0.90 (Bi), 0.60 (Bé), 0.35 (Be) and 0.20 (BNN), shifted on the logit scale by participant (SD 0.5) and item (SD 0.4) effects. Items are identified by their stem type; the nonce word forms are left out.

References

Hayes, B. & Londe, Z. C. (2006). Stochastic phonological knowledge: The case of Hungarian vowel harmony. Phonology, 23, 59-104. doi:10.1017/S0952675706000765

Hayes, B., Zuraw, K., Siptár, P. & Londe, Z. (2009). Natural and unnatural constraints in Hungarian vowel harmony. Language, 85, 822-863. doi:10.1353/lan.0.0169

Examples

round(prop.table(table(hungarian_harmony$stem_type, hungarian_harmony$suffix), 1), 2)
#>      
#>       back front
#>   B   0.97  0.03
#>   F   0.03  0.97
#>   N   0.10  0.90
#>   Bi  0.90  0.10
#>   Bé  0.57  0.43
#>   Be  0.40  0.60
#>   BNN 0.27  0.73
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  mixed <- subset(hungarian_harmony, is.element(stem_type, c("Bi", "Bé", "Be", "BNN")))
  m <- lme4::glmer(suffix ~ stem_type + (1 | participant) + (1 | item),
                   data = droplevels(mixed), family = binomial)
  lme4::fixef(m)
}
#>  (Intercept)  stem_typeBé  stem_typeBe stem_typeBNN 
#>    -2.412547     2.089060     2.851847     3.535148
